in.other_title: Persona-conditioned GPT-4o judges of debate reach 78.5% vs 70.1% for human judges
in.rationale: Khan et al. report humans have higher judge accuracy than LLM judges across all protocols on QuALITY HARD. Rahman et al. report default GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-7B debate judges are comparable to humans (69.8% and 70.7% vs 70.1%) and persona-based GPT-4o judges exceed them (up to 78.5%) on COVID-19 claims; domain, judge models and information conditions differ.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether human judges of AI debate are more accurate than LLM judges

open_obligations: Note that Michael et al.'s GPT-4 consultants were poor at arguing wrong answers, unlike Khan et al.'s optimised GPT-4-Turbo.
Check the size of Khan et al.'s incorrect-consultant accuracy drop.

out.other_title: Dishonest human consultants deceive judges 40% of the time; dishonest GPT-4 ones do not
out.rationale: Michael et al. report dishonest human consultants deceive judges 40% of the time on QuALITY-hard. Khan et al. report that in consultancy incorrect experts cause low human judge accuracy, suggesting it is easier to be misled in consultancy; Khan et al.'s consultants are GPT-4-Turbo, whereas Michael et al. found dishonest GPT-4 consultants did not mislead judges much (87% accuracy), so the support is for strong consultants.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether dishonest consultants mislead human judges in hidden-passage QuALITY consultancy

text: The paper reports that in consultancy, incorrect experts cause low human judge accuracy, suggesting it is easier to be misled in consultancy, and that humans have higher judge accuracy than LLM judges across all protocols. It finds identical judge accuracy between static and interactive debate and concludes that adding non-expert interaction does not help in information-asymmetric debates, which the authors call surprising.
title: Judge interaction does not raise human debate accuracy; incorrect consultants mislead
